title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The preceding page (102) finishes a small theory of correspondences between sets. A correspondence α between E and E' is a span E ← F → E' with legs f and f'. It acts on subsets by an operator α_* : P(E) → P(E'), which is the composite of pulling back along one leg and pushing forward along the other. Grothendieck lists equivalent conditions for several properties.
(A) α is an isomorphism iff α_* commutes with arbitrary intersections and with complement C.
(B) α_*(1_E) = 1_{E'} iff α_* reflects emptiness iff f' is surjective.
(Corollaries 2 and 3) α_* commutes 'faithfully' with the relation |∘|, which is presumably 'S meets T', i.e. S∩T ≠ ∅. Such conditions characterize α as a comorphism composed with an injective morphism, or as the comorphism of a surjection.
These are set-level, essentially Boolean results. Morphisms are spans read through power sets, and a complete Boolean algebra map P(E) → P(E') comes from a map E' → E.

This page asks a programmatic question. Do these equivalences keep a meaning, and stay valid, for correspondences between more general 'spaces'? The phrase is badly transcribed, but the next page speaks of 'spatios', a geometric interpretation and contractibility, so the target is spaces in a homotopical or stratified sense.
Grothendieck observes that without a factorization of the type α_* = f'^! f_*, the 'naive' or 'direct' interpretation in terms of properties of the legs f, f' is bound to disappear. What keeps a clear meaning are the algebraic equivalents: commutation with ∩, with complement, with |∘|, and the conditions 1 ↦ 1 and reflection of ∅.
He then notes a failure. The equivalence (ii) ⇔ (iii') of part A does not hold without 'draconian' hypotheses analogous to Boolean ones. These were already specified in the reminders about conditions (contractibility?) on supports.
He suggests this may be a false problem. For genuinely geometric work one restricts to very special supports, essentially constructible ones, which are stable under the operations. Under such conditions, of contractibility or 'commensurability', the arguments of A should work again. The next page continues: commutation of α_* with |∘| should mean an 'accomplishment' into a fibration (a homotopy equivalence followed by an injective fibration), and adding α_*(1) = 1 should give commutation with complement under contractibility conditions.
The margin refers to examples in an earlier chapter or file (VIII, 2-VI, p. 72).

Modern reading. The page is about the passage from relations between sets (Rel and its Boolean algebra of subsets) to a lattice-theoretic or 'pointless' setting. Lattice maps between algebras of supports replace spans of maps of points. Boolean-type properties such as complement-preservation and the meets-relation characterizations fail in general (Heyting or distributive setting) but can be recovered on a Boolean subalgebra of 'constructible' supports.
errors: No mathematical error is visible; the page states a question and an expected failure without proof.

The claims that the A-equivalences fail without Boolean-type hypotheses, and are restored for constructible supports under contractibility or 'commensurability' conditions, are only heuristic here; no argument is given on this page.

ideas.what: Replace correspondences (spans) between sets by their action on lattices of subsets/supports and keep only the algebraic characterizations (commutation with ∩, complement, 'meets' relation, 1↦1) when passing to general spaces
ideas.modern_name: relations as sup-lattice/frame maps; pointless (locale-theoretic) treatment of relations; Rel vs Sup
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tarski/Stone duality for Boolean case; locale theory (Ehresmann, Isbell, Joyal–Tierney 1984, Johnstone 'Stone Spaces' 1982)

ideas.what: Boolean-type equivalences fail for general spaces except under draconian hypotheses; restrict to constructible supports to recover them
ideas.modern_name: Boolean algebra of constructible sets in a stratified/o-minimal or 'tame' setting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Constructible sets: Chevalley/EGA; tame topology: Grothendieck's Esquisse (1984), van den Dries (o-minimality)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to the 'topologie modérée' theme of Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but the link is unsure

ideas.what: Conditions of contractibility/'commensurability' on supports making set-theoretic characterizations of correspondences survive (continued on next page as fibration-type interpretation)
ideas.modern_name: homotopy-theoretic analogue of factorization of correspondences (equivalence followed by fibration)

missed.claim: Programme to characterize correspondences between 'spaces' (in a stratified/tame sense) purely through their action on constructible supports. 'Meets'-preservation would correspond to a homotopy-equivalence-plus-fibration factorization. The analysis stops at stating the needed 'draconian' hypotheses and hoping constructibility removes them.
missed.quote: Peut-être [...] des faux problèmes, [...] des supports très particuliers [...] (constructibles)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: There is mild relevance to tame/o-minimal geometry and to recovering spaces and maps from Boolean algebras of definable sets. The thread is too sketchy here to count as a lost result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a reflective transition page. It notes that set-theoretic characterizations of correspondences need Boolean hypotheses for general spaces and suggests restricting to constructible supports. It is interesting as a window on Grothendieck's 1986 'spaces/supports' programme but contains no definite new result.
transcription_corrections: 'par une correspondance' should likely read 'pour une correspondance'.
'entre dispositions géminaux' is doubtful; it is probably 'entre espaces généraux' or similar, but it is illegible and should stay marked [?].
'Faute d'avoir une interprétation' is likely 'Faute d'avoir une décomposition' (or 'disponibilité') 'du type α_* = f'^! f_*'.
The supra-linear insertion reads approximately '(ou que (ii) équivaut à (iii) (iii'))', i.e. the equivalence (ii)⇔(iii') of A.
The phrase 'pas d'équivalence ... sans des hypothèses draconiennes, analogues des hypothèses booléennes' is correct in substance.

The line near the bottom is likely 'Peut-être sont-ce là de faux problèmes, en ce que pour un travail proprement géométrique, on travaille avec des supports très particuliers ... (essentiellement constructibles)'.
The last line likely reads 'ce sont, précisément, les arguments' (continuing to the next page).
